facts.fact: The Head introduces Phil to the staff room as the school's new Latin teacher, Miss Philomela Fen.
facts.anchor: our new Latin mistress, Miss Philomela Fen.

facts.fact: The history teacher introduces herself as Mirabel Grending and speaks with a hoarse voice punctuated by “hrr”.
facts.anchor: My name is Grending, Mirabel Grending

facts.fact: Dr Tregennis, the English teacher, is a very large man seated in a large armchair by the fireplace.
facts.anchor: And this is Dr Tregennis, our English teacher

facts.fact: Dr Tregennis tells Phil she should last longer than the previous Latin teacher Bredon.
facts.anchor: Hope you last longer than Bredon did

facts.fact: Miss Grending says Bredon kept bringing up the Templars, a topic that should be left to experts.
facts.anchor: she would always – hrr – bring up the Templars

facts.fact: Dr Tregennis guesses Bredon left over the school trophies and the appraisers being brought in to check the silver.
facts.anchor: the appraisers in, didn’t you, Head? Checking up on the silver?

facts.fact: The school librarian Miss Telfer is on compassionate leave after a grandparent's death; Smithson notes it is her fourth grandparent in a year.
facts.anchor: Miss Telfer, is currently on compassionate leave due to her grandparent’s death

facts.fact: Geography teacher Miss Knaresborough is off shopping on a free afternoon.
facts.anchor: Miss Knaresborough, is taking advantage of a free afternoon to do some shopping

facts.fact: After the girls storm the staff room, Phil sees Miss Grending slip a small gun back into her handbag.
facts.anchor: slipping a small gun back into her pretty handbag

facts.fact: Girls climbing to the first-floor staff-room window use grapnels to hook onto the carved stone windowsill.
The Head orders Virginia to bring all the girls to her study at half past six after supper.
facts.anchor: Virginia, be a good girl and bring everyone to my study at half past six tonight after supper

facts.fact: A doubly signed contract already exists and rests in the Head's desk, so Phil is already bound.
facts.anchor: that doubly signed contract which was now reposing in the Head’s desk

facts.fact: Jane Worth insists to Phil that she has not signed a contract yet and can still leave.
facts.anchor: You haven’t signed a contract yet, have you?

facts.fact: Mr Smithson warns Phil to watch out for pupil Muriel Tacks, who has been self-training as an electrician.
facts.anchor: Ever since she started self-training as an electrician, no chair near her has been safe

facts.fact: Music teacher Mr Tobenham lives a mile away and cycles in before dawn; art is taught by Mrs Samson, whom Smithson warns is “a little strange”.
facts.anchor: Music’s taken by Mr Tobenham, but he doesn’t actually live on school grounds

facts.fact: The Head advises Phil to be careful about bringing alcohol in, though she herself enjoys a gin and lime.
facts.anchor: be very careful about bringing any alcohol in with you
